chunks: Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty: 'Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful.'

He said: '[They are fearful] out of their concern and their hope; they fear that their deeds will be rejected if they do not obey Allah – and He has power over all things – and they hope that He accepts [their deeds] from them.'
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'with their hearts fearful' mean in Surah Al-Mu'minun?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse 'And those who give whatever they give with their hearts fearful' (Q23:60) by defining the spiritual state of the righteous as a balance of hope and fear. He explains that their 'fearfulness' stems from anxiety that their deeds may be rejected due to any deficiency in their obedience to God, while their 'hope' lies in the expectation that God will accept their efforts. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on *khawf* and *raja'* as complementary virtues that drive continuous self-reflection and devotion.
